newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end firmer on selective blue-chip buying.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end firmer on selective blue-chip buying.

text.p: Malaysian shares closed higher on Friday as institutional funds selectively bought blue-chip stocks cheapened by recent falls, dealers said.
By the close, the benchmark Composite Index of 100 leading issues gained 8.47 points, 0.76 percent, to 1,117.31.
"There were a few small buy programs in the market today, from foreign houses," said a dealer at BBMB Securities.

Infrastructure developer Renong fell 14 cents to 3.40 ringgit. Its share price was dogged by rumours that the company's liabilities would increase after the announcement of a put option on 112 million Time Engineering shares.
Telekom gained 10 cents to 12.50. On Wednesday the company was reported to be part of a Thai telecommunications joint venture with Samart Corp Plc.
Westmont Industries gained 20 cents to close at 2.88. Dealers and analysts said the stock may have been subject to a speculative play.
Market volume remained thin with 214 million shares traded. Gainers nosed out losers 290 to 268.
"The market is likely to remain in a narrow range next week, with the focus being on speculative stocks," said Soh Meng Hui, research manager at K.L. City Securities.
On the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange the spot June contract rose 9.1 points to 1,122.0 with 642 lots traded. No other contracts were traded.
